subtitle: Guidance from every product view, with source context preserved.

items.title: Use one term

items.title: Review the transformation
items.text: A fluent rewrite can still change meaning.

items.title: Short sentences
items.text: Keep sentences short. Preserve necessary conditions and uncertainty. Keep the original source beside the review view.

items.title: Active verbs
items.text: Use active voice. Name the person or component that performs each action.

items.title: Consistent terms
items.text: Use the same term for the same concept. Define technical terms when the audience needs them.

items.title: One main idea

items.title: Preserve meaning

items.title: STE-inspired writing
items.text: I used STE-inspired writing in this presentation. Each sentence carries one main idea. Full ASD-STE100 compliance has not been checked.

sections.title: Submission and human review
sections.summary: The agent proposes a record. The reviewer checks evidence, meaning and access before approval.

items.title: Check before review
items.text: Reject malformed input. Hold unsupported or conflicting claims.

items.title: Evidence review
items.text: Check sources, dates, scope and unsupported statements.

items.title: Meaning review
items.text: Check definitions, units, assumptions and conflicts.

items.title: Access review
items.text: Confirm workspace, permitted audience and purpose.

items.title: Version-bound approval
items.text: Bind the reviewer decision to the submitted content hash.

items.title: Derived claims
items.text: Send new interpretation through preparation and review.

items.title: Release ownership
items.text: An accountable owner accepts release and pilot evidence.

items.title: Submission + workspace
items.text: Resolve scope and duplicates.

items.title: Kind + proposed meaning
items.text: Preserve the dispute exception.

items.title: Source + version
items.text: Read the original evidence.

items.title: Validity + uncertainty
items.text: Verify dates and conflicting evidence.

items.title: Owner + access
items.text: Confirm reviewer and permitted audience.

items.title: Proposed links
items.text: Review new IDs and derived meaning.

items.title: Receive the submission
items.text: Accept one structured envelope with the original source, owner, scope and evidence. Treat source instructions as data.

items.title: Prepare two views
items.text: Application code checks the schema and rejects malformed input. A chosen model may propose the STE-inspired review view. Keep the original beside it.

items.title: Check meaning risks
items.text: Compare dates, units, negation, exceptions and obligation strength. Hold unsupported claims and possible meaning changes. These checks do not establish truth.

items.title: Ask the responsible human
items.text: The reviewer checks evidence, meaning and access. The reviewer may approve, request a revision or reject the submission.

items.title: Register the approved version
items.text: Record the canonical ID, content hash, reviewer and approved version. A changed record starts another preparation and review.

items.title: One definition
items.text: Reference one approved metric definition. Link it to canonical identity, owner and source revision.

items.title: Standing tests
items.text: Keep standing quality tests against owner-approved reference answers. A test pass supports only its tested scope.

items.title: Audit evidence
items.text: Preserve source, reviewer, date and exact version. Read back persistent evidence across the workflow.

items.title: Reviewed change
items.text: Reviewed learning: new drafts return to human review before an approved release.

items.title: Keep people in charge of priorities
items.text: Owners define priorities and acceptable trade-offs. A human reviews the evidence and approves an exact version. Model scores cannot replace that decision authority.

source.label: Keep people in charge of priorities · source

details.label: Analogy boundary
details.text: Owner-defined rules are explicit software inputs. The product does not gain empathy, emotions or moral judgment from this analogy.

source.label: Keep people in charge of priorities · boundary

items.title: Is the record complete?
items.text: Reject malformed data. Do not invent missing evidence.

items.title: Does the meaning match?
items.text: Hold unsupported or conflicting claims. Shorter English must not remove an exception or change a formula.

sections.title: Identity, versions and lifecycle
sections.summary: A canonical ID gives one object a stable identity. Versioned records link facts, measures, concepts, and meaning.

items.title: Resolve identity
items.text: Match the existing object before creating another canonical ID.

items.title: Bind the semantic source
items.text: For metrics, map the LookML model, Explore, view and measure to a Git revision.

items.title: Version the meaning
items.text: Keep the owner, approval, population, grain, unit, time window and exceptions with each version.

items.title: Enforce permissions
items.text: An ID locates a record. Recheck access for each consumer and source query.

items.title: Governed links
items.text: Derived records reference approved input IDs and versions.

items.title: Canonical records
items.text: Keep sources, approved versions, status and review history.

items.title: Corrections
items.text: Update or invalidate indexes after approved source changes, expiry, withdrawal or revoked access. Recheck canonical state before delivery. Preserve IDs, versions, formulas, units and validity dates.

items.title: Changed approved record
items.text: Require a new version and review. Keep the prior audit history.

items.title: Expired or withdrawn input
items.text: Invalidate dependent output, search indexes and cached views. Rebuild from approved releases. Block stale or revoked content at delivery.

items.title: Publication failure
items.text: Do not expose a partial update. Keep the prior release available only while it remains valid and permitted.

items.title: Resolve the approved identity
items.text: Match an existing canonical object before creating another ID. Load its approved version and permitted workspace.

items.title: Ask the organizer
items.text: The harness asks the chosen model for a typed category or link proposal. Code validates allowed categories, identity references and versions.

items.title: Build the versioned bundle
items.text: Link records to approved input IDs and versions. A Metric Passport retains the LookML project, model, Explore, view, measure and Git revision.

items.title: Return new meaning to review
items.text: A new interpretation or changed definition is a submission. Keep it out of the approved bundle until exact-version human review succeeds.

source.label: Return new meaning to review · source

items.title: Native source
items.text: Bind the metric to the approved LookML model, Explore, view, measure and Git revision. Reference the native formula or certified SQL revision.

items.title: Metric meaning
items.text: Keep the population, grain, unit, time window and exceptions together. Grain means the level represented by one data record.

items.title: Review evidence
items.text: Record the responsible reviewer and the exact approved version. Retain source evidence, validity and audit history.

items.title: Access rules
items.text: Resolve identity before creating another canonical ID. An ID grants no access. Recheck permissions for each consumer and source query.

items.title: Data
items.text: Preserve source facts, fields, values, dates, units and versions.

items.title: Metric
items.text: Bind the LookML project, model, Explore, view, measure and Git revision, or certified SQL revision. Keep population, grain, unit, period and exceptions. Preserve native calculation logic.

items.title: Ontology
items.text: An ontology defines concepts and their relationships. Link aliases to governed entity IDs.

items.title: Interpretation
items.text: Explain meaning under stated assumptions. New derived claims require human review and approved input references.

items.title: Review what changes
items.text: Record outcomes and source changes. Invalidate withdrawn or expired views. Return changed meaning to human review before reuse.

details.label: Analogy boundary
details.text: A feedback log is not biological learning. Changed meaning still needs approval; a successful output does not make it true.

items.title: Hold publication
items.text: Do not publish a derived object whose evidence or dependency is invalid. Resubmit changed meaning.

items.title: Did publication succeed?
items.text: A completed write request is not proof of a valid release.

items.title: Use valid prior release
items.text: If no valid prior release exists, hold delivery. Repair the publication fault and retry.

items.title: Has source state changed?
items.text: A lifecycle event can occur after delivery. Revoke invalid views immediately; approve changed meaning before reuse.

items.title: Invalidate dependent views
items.text: Rebuild indexes only from current approved releases. A source change that changes meaning must also become a reviewed submission.

sections.title: Retrieval and bounded orchestration
sections.summary: A context vault is a workspace with controlled records and access rules. A consumer receives a permitted view, not the whole vault.

items.title: Calibration
items.text: Check reported probabilities against observed outcomes before using risk thresholds.

items.title: Retrieval route
items.text: Use exact ID lookup first when identity is known. Otherwise combine keyword and semantic search, or follow approved links. Code enforces permissions independently of model signals.

items.title: Choice
items.text: Select one category from an allowed list.

items.title: Yes / no
items.text: Judge a defined condition. Policy checks still enforce access.

items.title: Rubric score
items.text: Rate a property against stated criteria. A score is not a probability.

items.title: Working context
items.text: Load relevant subject matter expert (SME) knowledge within the request budget.

items.title: Derived views
items.text: Build a rebuildable index of approved descriptions and linked evidence. Hybrid search combines keyword matches and semantic similarity. An embedding is a numerical representation used to compare meaning.

items.title: Scope the request
items.text: Authenticate the caller. Restrict the workspace and records before retrieval. Natural-language questions do not need STE formatting.

items.title: Use an exact identifier
items.text: When the canonical ID and version are known, use deterministic lookup. A model call is not required.

items.title: Search words and meaning
items.text: Hybrid search combines keyword matches and semantic similarity. Search approved descriptions and linked evidence. An embedding is a numerical representation used to compare meaning.

items.title: Follow approved relationships
items.text: Use approved links for related context. Each linked record needs its own permission and validity check.

items.title: Resolve and bound the result
items.text: Resolve candidates to current canonical records. Recheck access, approval, units, period and validity. Return IDs, versions, evidence and limits within budget.

source.label: Resolve and bound the result · source

items.title: Hold unsupported interpretation
items.text: An optional model may supply choice, yes/no or rubric signals. Code validates them. Hold ambiguity and return new meaning or conflicts to human review. Routine permitted retrieval needs no new approval.

items.title: Choice
items.text: Select one category from an allowed list. Reject invalid output and keep access enforcement outside the model.

items.title: Yes / no
items.text: Judge a defined condition. Reported confidence cannot grant access or bypass human review.

items.title: Rubric score
items.text: Rate a property against stated criteria. A score is not a probability. Check reported probabilities against observed outcomes before using risk thresholds.

items.title: Derived views
items.text: Build derived views only when the use case needs them. Invalidate them when inputs expire, change or lose access. A cache is not an approval authority.

items.title: Working context
items.text: Load relevant subject matter expert knowledge within the request budget. Deliver approved query references for familiar tasks. Prepare and review expert drafts for new meaning.

items.title: Triage
items.text: Route defined work through a qualified path. Escalate new or uncertain meaning for review.

items.title: Hold the right task context
items.text: Keep the current goal, permitted evidence and task state available. The proposed orchestration code limits the context and work budget.

source.label: Hold the right task context · source

details.label: Analogy boundary
details.text: A context window is a software resource. It does not reproduce biological working memory or store the whole knowledge base.

source.label: Hold the right task context · boundary

items.title: Choose an allowed path
items.text: Choose an allowed retrieval path: exact ID, hybrid search or approved relationships. Request clarification when evidence is insufficient. Keep every route within the permitted scope.

details.label: Analogy boundary
details.text: The router follows engineered rules and evaluated signals. This mapping does not claim human planning or an optimal choice.

items.title: Stop invalid work
items.text: Keep the failure visible. Correct the input or model response before another attempt.

items.title: Follow approved links
items.text: Follow only approved relationships. Check access on every linked record.

items.title: Is the evidence sufficient?
items.text: Do not turn the nearest match into an unsupported answer.

items.title: Resolve canonical records
items.text: Treat index hits as candidates. Resolve their source IDs and versions before delivery.

items.title: Within the response budget?
items.text: Preserve evidence and material exceptions. Do not silently trim meaning to fit.

items.title: Narrow or hold the request
items.text: A revised request passes through access checks again.

source.label: Narrow or hold the request · source

sections.title: Access, delivery and failure handling
sections.summary: The MCP server exposes permitted context. The server must enforce the product’s record and workspace policies.

items.title: Structured output
items.text: Return IDs, versions, evidence, validity and unresolved limits.

items.title: Access at use
items.text: Authorize and filter before retrieval. Resolve candidates to canonical records. Recheck current permissions, versions, approval and validity before delivery.

items.title: Bounded search response
items.text: Return only permitted context. Treat empty or ambiguous matches as a hold or clarification. A similarity score cannot approve a claim.

items.title: Invalid or missing evidence
items.text: Reject malformed data. Hold unsupported claims for revision.

references.label: Invalid or missing evidence · parallel source

items.title: Uncertain or conflicting meaning
items.text: Record the conflict. Ask the responsible reviewer.

references.label: Uncertain or conflicting meaning · parallel source

items.title: Denied consumer access
items.text: Return a controlled denial. Do not leak restricted record content.

items.title: Empty or ambiguous search
items.text: Return a controlled hold or clarification. Route new interpretation or conflicting meaning to human review.

items.title: Verify and restrict
items.text: Authenticate the caller. Enforce workspace, purpose and record permissions before retrieval. Deny the request without exposing restricted text.

items.title: Find permitted candidates
items.text: Use exact ID lookup, hybrid search or approved links within the permitted scope. Empty or ambiguous results return a controlled hold or clarification.

items.title: Recheck current canonical records
items.text: Resolve candidates to canonical IDs and versions. Check current permission, approval, validity and complete release state. Exclude expired, withdrawn or revoked records.

items.title: Return a bounded bundle
items.text: Return permitted IDs, versions, evidence, validity and unresolved limits through MCP. Do not expose a partial release. Reuse a prior release only if it is still valid and permitted.

items.title: Review changes and repair views
items.text: New meaning returns to submission and human review. Source updates, withdrawal and expiry invalidate dependent indexes. Rebuild from approved releases. Routine search does not approve records.

source.label: Review changes and repair views · source

items.title: Certified logic
items.text: Deliver approved query references for native execution. Recheck authorization, data validity and execution conditions.

items.title: Policy gate
items.text: Check delivery permissions. The consumer must enforce its own source access and execution policies.

items.title: MCP and application authorization
items.text: MCP defines context exchange. Authentication and application authorization still require implementation. The protocol alone does not make a product secure.

items.title: Stop at the permission gate
items.text: Check permission before retrieval. Stop the request when its scope fails policy. Recheck current records before delivery. Code enforces these gates.

source.label: Stop at the permission gate · source

details.label: Analogy boundary
details.text: Stopping a movement and denying data access are different mechanisms. The analogy explains restraint; it does not establish security.

source.label: Stop at the permission gate · boundary

items.title: May we accept this source?
items.text: Admission policy runs outside the model. An available connector is not permission.

source.label: May we accept this source? · source

items.title: Deny admission
items.text: Record a permitted audit receipt. A source owner must resolve access before another submission.

items.title: Receive a context request
items.text: Resolve caller, workspace, purpose and requested context. The request does not inherit the submitter’s permissions.

items.title: Deny restricted access
items.text: No title, excerpt or record body may leak through a failed access check.

items.title: Consumer uses the context
items.text: Context delivery does not authorize a purchase, message, trade or other external action.

sections.title: Component qualification and release
sections.summary: Versioned contracts let us evaluate new models, retrieval systems and interfaces while preserving governed context.

items.title: Qualification cost
items.text: Budget evaluation, migration, rollback and maintenance.

items.title: Describe one candidate change
items.text: Identify the model, index or adapter, version and affected interface. Keep the current approved release available.

items.title: Plan the comparison
items.text: The coordinator selects agreed held-out cases and failure scenarios. Compare the same approved inputs, permissions and expected outcomes.

items.title: Test the contract
items.text: Check meaning, exceptions, evidence, access, full cost and service behavior. The current browser rehearsal tests deterministic examples only.

items.title: Ask the release owner
items.text: An accountable owner reviews persistent qualification evidence. A failed check or missing evidence retains the current compatible release.

items.title: Publish or roll back
items.text: Publish a complete validated release only after owner acceptance. Invalidate affected views. Use a tested rollback when a release problem appears.

items.title: Keep the contract
items.text: Preserve meaning, source evidence, conditions, permissions and version rules across component changes.

items.title: Connect a candidate
items.text: Connect the candidate behind a versioned interface. A familiar interface does not prove compatible behavior.

items.title: Compare outcomes
items.text: Test evidence loss, exception loss and expanded permission alongside a compatible scenario. The browser rehearsal uses deterministic examples. Real qualification requires implementation, persistent evidence and authenticated readback.

items.title: Release or retain
items.text: Release only after owner acceptance. Retain the prior compatible release on failure. Budget evaluation, migration, rollback and maintenance. Invalidate affected caches.

items.title: Browser rehearsal evidence
items.text: A browser rehearsal demonstrates the intended contract. It does not validate a model, server, database or operational outcome.

sections.title: Pilot, acceptance and delivery plan
sections.summary: Run a baseline and a candidate on the same workload. Use held-out cases and complete cost evidence.

items.title: A funded proof of value
items.text: Start with one workflow. Measure the return before expansion.

source.label: A funded proof of value · source

items.title: Retrieval trial
items.text: Compare exact and keyword lookup with hybrid search on held-out questions. Test paraphrases, wrong units or periods, empty matches, ambiguity, expiry, revocation, cross-vault access and source-update rebuilds. Measure relevance, incorrect matches, latency, full cost and access-control results. Agree thresholds with the owner before testing.

items.title: Intake + requirements
items.text: Name the workflow and owners. Reuse catalog components. Map sources, baseline cost and success criteria.

items.title: Product design
items.text: Approve the context contract, Metric Passport, review duties, success gates and pilot budget.

items.title: Development
items.text: Build one complete context path. Reuse LookML and verify one consumer adapter.

items.title: Testing
items.text: Check owner-approved gold truth, standing QA, permissions and cost. Require security and leadership go/no-go.

items.title: Launch
items.text: Publish only the accepted release. Confirm operating owners, support and rollback.

items.title: Maintenance
items.text: Review corrections and drift. Requalify source or model changes before expanding.

items.title: Agree the contract
items.text: Reuse existing solutions. Set source bindings, reviewer authority, output schema and success gates.

items.title: Implement admission
items.text: Use one custom-app workflow to submit, review, version and persist an approved record.

items.title: Link and publish
items.text: Build its layer references and publish an atomic approved release.

items.title: Consume securely
items.text: Verify one consumer adapter. Check identity, permissions and bounded context delivery.

items.title: Test failure paths
items.text: Exercise rejection, conflict, withdrawal, expiry and failed publication.

items.title: Measure and decide
items.text: Compare accepted-task cost, quality and latency. Expand only after owner acceptance.

items.title: Pilot deliverable
items.text: A reusable context release linked to LookML, plus replayable acceptance evidence.

items.title: Buyer contribution
items.text: One workflow, source owner, baseline, reviewer time and permitted test access.

items.title: Investment decision
items.text: Approve a setup ceiling, recurring budget and named delivery responsibilities.

items.title: Expansion decision
items.text: Accept the result only when economics, quality and control meet the agreed gates.

items.title: Agree the test and thresholds
items.text: Agree owner thresholds first. Include paraphrases, exact IDs, wrong units or periods, empty matches, stale records, revoked access and cross-vault requests.

source.label: Agree the test and thresholds · source

items.title: Run both paths
items.text: Compare exact and keyword lookup with hybrid search. Use the same held-out tasks, approved records and access rules. Count retries and review queues.

items.title: Collect comparable evidence
items.text: Measure relevance, incorrect matches, full cost, latency and access behavior against owner-reviewed records. Preserve failed results.

items.title: Review the evidence
items.text: The owner checks thresholds, audit readback and remaining limits. An agent report is evidence, not approval.

items.title: Accept a bounded next step
items.text: Expand only within accepted scope and budget. Recheck changed components before wider use.

source.label: Accept a bounded next step · source

items.title: Hold and correct gaps
items.text: Missing evidence or a material access failure blocks expansion. Resolve the cause and rerun affected cases.

items.title: Name the problem and owners
items.text: Intake/Vetting selects one workflow. Product Requirements records source owners, baseline, scope and acceptance criteria.

source.label: Name the problem and owners · source

items.title: Approve the design and budget
items.text: Product Design defines the context contract, reviewer duties, access boundaries and funding ceiling. Reuse catalog components.

source.label: Approve the design and budget · source

items.title: Build one complete path
items.text: Development connects submission, human review, persistent layers and authenticated readback through one consumer adapter.

items.title: Test the product and its failures
items.text: Testing compares the baseline and candidate. Exercise rejection, stale data, conflict, withdrawal and failed publication.

source.label: Test the product and its failures · source

items.title: Launch only the accepted release
items.text: Security review and leadership go/no-go precede Launch. Name the operating owner and verify support and rollback.

source.label: Launch only the accepted release · source

items.title: Maintain and requalify changes
items.text: Maintenance checks drift, cost and value. New meaning returns to review. Source or model changes need qualification before expansion.

items.title: Intake / vetting
items.text: Name the workflow and sponsor. Check the solution, agent, skill and MCP catalogs before custom development.

items.title: Requirements
items.text: Map source definitions, current costs and permitted use. Agree technical and business success criteria.

items.title: Cost · trial
items.text: Compare the same accepted-task target. Record token and query charges, allocated and incremental licenses, adapters, operations and human handling without double counting.

items.title: Cost · acceptance
items.text: Expand only when the agreed economic case holds after full cost readback.

items.title: Performance · trial
items.text: Measure submit-to-approved-delivery latency and consuming-task completion separately. Include review queues and p95 at agreed load.

items.title: Performance · acceptance
items.text: Meet the owner’s service target without hiding failed, queued or held tasks.

items.title: Accuracy · trial
items.text: Test held-out questions against approved LookML definitions and owner-reviewed gold truth. Check grain, unit, time window and exceptions.

items.title: Accuracy · acceptance
items.text: Meet agreed quality gates. Investigate failures before expanding scope.

items.title: Trust · trial
items.text: Test source and consumer access, revoked permissions, hostile instructions, cross-vault retrieval and exact-version audit readback.

items.title: Trust · acceptance
items.text: Hold release for a material access failure. Assess user confidence separately.

items.title: Runtime evidence boundary
items.text: Diagram and browser checks establish presentation behavior only. No production runtime or measured customer benefit is established here.

items.title: Pilot and expansion approval
items.text: Approval funds a scoped pilot. Expansion requires a separate evidence-based decision. Price, dates and thresholds remain to agree.

items.title: Performance
items.text: Use bounded decisions and fast paths. Escalate when the task needs more work.

items.title: Performance · boundary
items.text: p95 is the time within which 95% of measured tasks finish. Compare the same workload and quality gates.

items.title: Accuracy
items.text: Carry source links, dates, conditions and conflicts. Check derived statements.

items.title: Accuracy · boundary
items.text: Abstention means withholding a conclusion when evidence is insufficient. A correct format does not prove a correct answer.

items.title: Trust
items.text: Enforce scope and permission. Show the evidence, owner and review decision.

items.title: Trust · boundary
items.text: Measure user confidence separately from correctness. Model confidence cannot create authority.

items.title: Record outcome and cost
items.text: Measure cost, latency, accuracy and access behavior. The owner decides pilot acceptance; no savings are proven by this diagram.

sections.title: Cost discipline and full economics
sections.summary: Choose the method, bound each call and verify reuse. Keep the same quality and access gates.

items.title: Setup
items.text: Record contract, source mapping, adapters, deployment and acceptance tests. Include initial embeddings and search index creation.

items.title: Recurring platform
items.text: Tokens, warehouse queries, storage, tools, delivery and monitoring. Include query embeddings, search and optional result ranking.

items.title: Human operations
items.text: Submission review, conflict resolution, corrections and incident handling.

items.title: Maintenance
items.text: Licenses, seats, source updates, access changes, upgrades and recovery. Include index updates, rebuilds and invalidation.

items.title: Reuse approved code or SQL
items.text: Use deterministic logic for defined rules. Keep certified queries unchanged. Review expert drafts before reuse.

source.label: Reuse approved code or SQL · source

references.label: Reuse approved code or SQL · parallel source

items.title: Bound context and output
items.text: Limit permitted context, tokens, output, steps and retries. Batch work only when its deadline permits.

references.label: Bound context and output · parallel source

items.title: Reuse valid context
items.text: Check cache version, expiry, access and invalidation. Measure hit rate, writes, reads and storage.

items.title: Qualify the model route
items.text: Use a smaller model only if it passes the task gates. Escalate uncertain results.

references.label: Qualify the model route · parallel source

items.title: Control warehouse cost
items.text: Estimate query work. For BigQuery on-demand queries, test maximum bytes billed. A row limit alone may not bound scans.

items.title: Count every cost once
items.text: Track tokens, queries, seats, licenses and human review. Assign budget owners. Separate existing and incremental costs. Count index build, update, storage and query costs once. Enter observed search charges into the existing platform and setup totals; source model rates remain unchanged.

items.title: Define one comparison target
items.text: Agree the same workload and number of accepted tasks for baseline and candidate. Record acceptance rates and review effort.

items.title: Choose a qualified route
items.text: Use approved code or SQL where suitable. Reuse valid approved context. Use a smaller model only after task qualification. Bound tokens, queries, steps and retries.

items.title: Count permitted execution
items.text: Count model, search, ranking, warehouse and delivery work. Include cache reads and writes. Measure each charge; do not assume savings.

items.title: Count human handling
items.text: Include review, rework, conflicts and incidents. Hold tasks that fail quality or access. An inexpensive rejected task is not an accepted result.

items.title: Count only accepted results
items.text: Use owner-defined acceptance gates. Include failed attempts and retries in the costs required to reach the same accepted-task target.

items.title: Compare the full cost
items.text: Separate setup from recurring cost. Include initial index build, updates, rebuilds, storage and queries. Allocate each charge once. Keep existing costs distinct from added spending.

items.title: Full cost
items.text: Track tokens, queries, seats, licenses and human review. Assign budget owners. Separate existing and incremental costs.

items.title: Comparable cost allocation
items.text: Separate existing allocated costs from incremental spending. Include both consistently in the baseline and candidate. Count each cost once.

items.title: Full cost scope
items.text: Digital cost includes model tokens, retrieval, warehouse queries, tools and variable infrastructure per attempt. Handling includes review, rework and escalation. Fixed cost includes seats, licenses, adapters and operations. Compare existing and incremental costs consistently; count each once. Setup stays separate.

items.title: Illustrative assumptions
items.text: Invented example assumptions, not a quote or measured savings. The neutral starting case assumes no improvement. Rates and workload stay constant for the annual estimate. Validate the inputs and all quality gates.

items.title: Match the task to a qualified budget.
items.text: Compare cost per person and per team. Inspect model size, thinking, output and cache settings. Choose a cheaper route only after it passes the task gates.

source.label: Match the task to a qualified budget. · source

items.title: Task guidance status
items.text: The source settings and task recommendations are reference examples, not approved policy. Provider settings differ. The full-cost worksheet follows this model-only estimate.

items.title: Cost
items.text: Bound context size. Reuse valid views. Choose a capable route.

items.title: Cost · boundary
items.text: Include review, rework, retrieval and operations. Token savings alone do not establish value.

items.title: Source calculation limitation 1
items.text: Cache share is an assumption. Confirm eligible prefixes, expiry, writes and storage with your provider.

items.title: Source calculation limitation 2
items.text: The retry input adds an expected cost allowance. It does not simulate additional calls.

items.title: Source calculation limitation 3
items.text: The source simple comparison prices the question and answer only. It excludes tools, context, history and thinking.

items.title: Source calculation limitation 4
items.text: The source Flash example uses a future full rate. Its Pro example omits the stated long-context tier. Enter the rate that applies to your workload.

items.title: Source calculation limitation 5
items.text: All non-question input is cache-eligible in the source calculation. Check each real provider prefix. The first-call write premium uses the full instructions, tools and document prefix.

items.title: Source calculation limitation 6
items.text: Instruction, document and tool token fields are baseline estimates. Set the tokenizer factor to 1 for measured target-model token counts.

items.title: Source calculation limitation 7
items.text: The question-and-answer comparison applies the selected tokenizer and region factors consistently. This corrects omissions in the source comparison. It is not a return-on-investment baseline.

sections.title: Motion and reading
sections.summary: Use motion to show what changed, where context moves, and why it stops. Keep the text still while people read. Add depth to diagrams when it helps explain their layers.

items.title: Motion purpose
items.text: Use motion to show what changed, where context moves, and why it stops. Keep the text still while people read. Add depth to diagrams when it helps explain their layers.

items.title: Stage handoff
items.text: Use a brief exit and arrival when a slide changes. Keep navigation immediate. Preserve the 16-slide print deck.

items.title: Reading focus
items.text: Keep the diagram beside the current explanation. Use bounded depth. Preserve all 16 chapters and 31 topics.

items.title: Route continuity
items.text: Highlight the selected node and its outcomes. Move only along its routes. Preserve all 57 nodes and 70 routes.

items.title: Connected explanation
items.text: Link each brain function to the software analogy. Keep source references and scientific limits in place.

items.title: Shared rules for every direction
items.text: Pause stops all motion. Flat view removes depth only. Reduced motion shows a readable static state. Narrow screens use flat diagrams. Off-screen diagrams stop. The implementation will use the existing native CSS, SVG and shared animation clock.

source.label: Shared rules for every direction · source

items.title: Submit source context.
items.text: Collect a clear description and linked evidence. Keep the source text available. This sample preserves the intended process.

items.title: Review before approval.
items.text: A human reviews the submission. Missing evidence returns to the review process. A model recommendation cannot grant permission.

items.title: Keep one source of truth.
items.text: Store the approved canonical record. A canonical record is the authoritative version. A search index remains a rebuildable copy.

items.title: Check before delivery.
items.text: Find relevant context. Recheck caller access and current validity. Deliver a bounded bundle through the proposed MCP service.
